title: Step Into Another World: How Virtual Reality Goes Beyond Entertainment
title_zh: 踏入另一个世界：虚拟现实如何超越娱乐
intro_zh: 本文约900词，包含6个重点词汇。文章围绕虚拟现实技术在教育、职业培训、医疗康复、文化体验和人际理解等领域的实际应用展开，内容贴近生活，难度适中，适合CET-4学习者阅读。

paragraphs.en: Have you ever dreamed of walking on the moon or swimming with dolphins without leaving your living room? Virtual reality (VR), a computer technology that creates a lifelike three-dimensional world, turns such dreams into possible experiences. Using a headset and motion sensors, users can look around and interact with a digital environment as if it were real. For many years, VR was mainly used for gaming. Today, however, its range is much wider. From pilot training programs to virtual tours of famous museums, VR is becoming a valuable tool in our daily lives. This immersive medium is opening doors that once seemed locked.
paragraphs.zh: 你曾经梦想过不用离开客厅就能在月球上行走或与海豚一起游泳吗？虚拟现实（VR），一种创造逼真三维世界的计算机技术，正将这样的梦想变成可能的体验。使用头戴式显示器和运动传感器，用户可以环顾四周并与虚拟环境互动，就像在真实世界中一样。多年来，VR主要用于游戏。但如今，它的应用范围广泛得多。从飞行员培训项目到著名博物馆的虚拟游览，VR正成为我们日常生活中的宝贵工具。这种沉浸式的媒介正打开一扇扇曾经看似紧锁的大门。

paragraphs.en: In education, VR breathes life into subjects that students often find dry. Instead of merely reading about volcanoes, children can simulate a volcanic eruption in a science lesson. A 2020 study from Stanford University found that middle school students who learned with VR scored 30 percent higher on memory tests than those who used traditional materials. At Georgia Tech, engineering students build bridges in a virtual laboratory and test them under different weather conditions. They change the design and instantly see how the bridge holds up. This direct experience with cause and effect makes abstract ideas concrete and learning far more engaging.
paragraphs.zh: 在教育领域，VR让那些学生常觉得枯燥的科目焕发生机。学生不再仅仅阅读火山的描述，而是可以在科学课上模拟火山喷发。斯坦福大学2020年的一项研究发现，用VR学习的中学生在记忆测试中比使用传统材料的学生得分高30%。在佐治亚理工学院，工程专业的学生在虚拟实验室中建造桥梁，并在不同的天气条件下进行测试。他们改变设计，立刻就能看到桥梁的承受情况。这种对因果关系的直接体验让抽象的概念变得具体，也让学习更加引人入胜。

paragraphs.en: Beyond schools, VR is transforming workplace training. In high-risk jobs, machines and procedures can be practiced safely before stepping into the real world. For instance, firefighter trainees wear VR headsets to enter a burning building without breathing a puff of smoke. They must decide where to spray water and how to rescue trapped people. Companies like Walmart have also used VR to prepare employees for stressful events, such as the Black Friday rush. Employee response time was cut by nearly half after a short VR rehearsal. Likewise, surgeons rehearse delicate operations on virtual patients. This kind of practice saves money, reduces accidents, and gives workers confidence.
paragraphs.zh: 除了学校，VR正在改变职场培训。在高风险工作中，人员和设备操作可以在进入现实世界之前安全地进行练习。例如，消防实习生戴上VR头显，在不吸入一口烟雾的情况下进入燃烧的建筑物。他们必须决定在哪里喷水以及如何营救被困人员。像沃尔玛这样的公司也用VR让员工为“黑色星期五”抢购等压力事件做准备。经过短暂的VR预演，员工的反应时间几乎缩短了一半。同样，外科医生可以在虚拟病人身上练习精细手术。这种练习节省开支、减少事故，并增强员工信心。

paragraphs.en: In medicine, VR has moved from novelty to a genuine healing tool. For patients recovering from a stroke, repeating arm movements can be boring and painful. VR turns these exercises into games, where patients control a virtual bird flying through waterfalls. A hospital in Los Angeles reported that stroke survivors who used VR therapy showed 40 percent better hand movement after eight weeks. VR also helps calm patients during painful wound dressing. By taking their minds to a relaxing beach, doctors reduce pain without extra drugs. This new form of therapy is especially helpful for children and older adults because it feels more like play than treatment.
paragraphs.zh: 在医学中，VR已经从新鲜事物转变为真正的治疗工具。对于中风康复中的患者来说，重复的手臂运动可能枯燥而痛苦。VR将这些练习变成游戏，患者控制一只虚拟小鸟飞过瀑布。洛杉矶一家医院报告称，使用VR疗法的中风幸存者在八周后手部活动能力改善了40%。VR还有助于在疼痛的伤口包扎过程中安抚患者。通过将他们的注意力引向一片宁静的海滩，医生可以在不增加药物的情况下减轻疼痛。这种新形式的疗法对儿童和老年人尤其有帮助，因为它更像玩耍而不是治疗。

paragraphs.en: VR also breaks down geographical and physical barriers. People who cannot travel far due to age, illness, or budget can visit distant wonders. The British Museum, for example, offers a free VR tour that lets users walk among Egyptian mummies. In China, the Palace Museum has created an online virtual experience where scrolls and statues can be observed closely. Even real travel agencies now use VR to give customers a preview of hotels and cruises, which helps them make better choices. By making famous destinations more accessible, VR inspires curiosity and cultural appreciation. It can even revive memories for elderly people, who may experience familiar hometown scenes decades after leaving them.
paragraphs.zh: VR还打破了地理和身体上的障碍。那些因年龄、疾病或预算而无法远行的人，可以参观遥远的奇观。例如，大英博物馆提供免费的VR导览，让用户能够在埃及木乃伊之间行走。在中国，故宫博物院创建了一个在线虚拟体验，可以近距离观察卷轴和雕像。甚至实体旅行社现在也使用VR让顾客预览酒店和邮轮，帮助他们做出更明智的选择。通过让著名景点更容易到达，VR激发人们的好奇心和文化欣赏。它甚至还能唤起老年人的记忆，让他们在离开家乡几十年后重新体验熟悉的地方。

paragraphs.en: Less obvious but equally powerful is VR's ability to promote understanding between people. Through a technique called perspective-taking, users can step into the shoes of another person. For instance, an award-winning project called 'Be Another Lab' uses VR to let a man experience life as a woman, and a healthy person as someone in a wheelchair. Such experiments increase empathy and reduce prejudice. In classrooms, students may spend ten minutes as a poor old person facing daily discrimination. Researchers find that after a short VR session, donations to social causes increase and negative attitudes soften. This ability to feel others' situations could make us kinder, more patient citizens.
paragraphs.zh: 不太明显但同样强大的是VR促进人与人之间理解的能力。通过一种称为“视角转换”的技术，用户能够设身处地。例如，一个名为“Be Another Lab”的获奖项目利用VR让一名男性体验女性的生活，让健全人体验坐轮椅的人的生活。这样的实验能增进同理心并减少偏见。在课堂上，学生可能花十分钟扮演一位每天面对歧视的贫困老人。研究人员发现，经过短暂的VR会话，人们对社会事业的捐款增加，负面态度有所缓和。这种感受他人处境的能力，能让我们成为更友善、更有耐心的公民。

paragraphs.en: Despite its promise, VR still has obstacles to overcome. The most obvious is cost—a high-quality headset and computer can cost several thousand dollars. In addition, some individuals feel sick or dizzy after wearing heavy headsets, which doctors call 'simulator sickness'. For these reasons, many organizations remain reluctant to invest heavily in the technology. There are also social worries. If people spend too much time in exciting virtual worlds, real-life conversation and outdoor activities may suffer. However, engineers are designing lighter headsets and sharper displays. As prices continue to drop, these barriers will likely weaken, and VR could become a standard part of education and healthcare.
paragraphs.zh: 尽管前景广阔，VR仍有许多障碍需要克服。最明显的是成本——高质量的头显和电脑可能花费数千美元。此外，有些人在佩戴沉重的头显后会感到恶心或头晕，医生称之为“模拟器眩晕症”。出于这些原因，许多组织仍然不愿意在这项技术上大量投资。还有社会担忧。如果人们在刺激的虚拟世界中花费太多时间，现实生活中的交流和户外活动可能会减少。然而，工程师正在设计更轻的头显和更清晰的显示器。随着价格持续下降，这些障碍可能会减弱，VR可能成为教育和医疗的标准组成部分。

paragraphs.en: In less than a decade, virtual reality has grown from a futuristic fantasy to a practical everyday tool. It helps children learn faster, workers train safer, patients recover more comfortably, and citizens understand one another better. Of course, no headset can replace the warmth of a handshake or the beauty of a sunset. But VR offers a valuable extra layer of experience, especially when physical presence is impossible. The keys are to use it wisely and to keep human needs at the center. When we do that, putting on the headset becomes a step into a richer, more connected world.
paragraphs.zh: 在不到十年的时间里，虚拟现实已经从未来的幻想成长为实用的日常工具。它帮助孩子学得更快，工人训练得更安全，病人恢复得更舒适，公民更好地相互理解。当然，没有任何头显能够取代握手的温暖或日落的美丽。但VR提供了一种宝贵的额外体验，尤其是在无法亲临现场的时候。关键在于明智地使用它，并始终把人类的需求放在核心位置。当我们这样做了，戴上头显就成为迈向一个更丰富、更互联世界的一步。

questions.q: What is the main idea of the article?
options: Virtual reality is mainly used for entertainment and video games.
Virtual reality is now applied to many aspects of daily life beyond games.
Virtual reality technology is still too expensive for most people.
Virtual reality will replace traditional teaching methods completely.
questions.explain: 文章围绕VR不再只是游戏技术，而是广泛应用于教育、医疗、职业培训、文化体验等多方面，因此B正确。A片面，C只是文中提到的挑战之一，D过于绝对。

questions.q: According to the passage, how does VR help surgeons improve their skills?
options: They can practice complex operations on virtual patients.
They can watch videos of real operations online.
They can use VR to operate on real patients safely.
They can charge patients less for VR-based surgery.
questions.explain: 第三段提到外科医生可以在虚拟病人身上排练精细手术，因此A正确。B未提及；C错误，因为不是对真实患者操作；D未提费用。

questions.q: What can we infer from the last paragraph?
options: VR should completely replace direct human experience.
VR should be used wisely with human needs as the priority.
VR is not helpful for interpersonal communication.
VR will sooner or later disappear from education.
questions.explain: 末段强调VR不能替代真实体验，关键在于明智使用并把人类需求放在中心，因此推断B正确。A与作者观点相反；C与末段“相互理解更好”不符；D无支持。

questions.q: What does the word reluctant in Paragraph 7 most probably mean?
questions.explain: reluctant 意为“不情愿的”，对应选项B unwilling and hesitant。
